caption.verbatim: Figure 1: Evaluation framework

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 1: Evaluation framework
items.note: A five-rank box diagram: Ecosystem (purple) into Support Service (grey), which feeds a horizontal bus that reaches Supply Service, Adjustment Service and Cultural Service (dark green), which in turn feed Direct Value, Indirect Value and Existing Value (mid green), which converge on Total Value (pale green). Two double-headed blue arrows stand in for axes - 'Time & Space Scale' across the top and 'Ecological service value assessment process' down the left - and there is no other legend. THE DIAGRAM CONTRADICTS THE TEXT IT SERVES: section 3.3 says support services are 'the backbone' and 'we recommend not evaluating support services to avoid double the value', but the framework draws Support Service on the same rank as the three valued services and routes it through the same bus into the value layer. THE ARROWS DO NOT RESOLVE: the bus under Support Service splits three ways and drops into Adjustment Service from above while the two outer services take their feed from the same bus at a different height, and the Supply Service arrow crosses the Cultural Service arrow's drop - so the graph draws at least one crossing that no rendering makes meaningful. The three value boxes touch their neighbours' strokes, the Adjustment Service box overprints the line beneath it, and no box carries a step number although the citing sentence says 'the main workﬂow involved consists of four steps'. Caption prints BELOW and the numbered-list marker '1.' of the following paragraph is welded to its tail in the text layer.

caption.verbatim: Figure 2: The basic equivalents of different ecosystem types and different value categories

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 2: The basic equivalents of different ecosystem types and different value categories
items.note: A value-coefficient grid printed and captioned as a figure: two header bands over FOURTEEN numeric value columns (Cultivated land, Woodland, Grassland, Farmland, Wetland, Waters, Unutilized land and the sub-types above them), with the left stub in three blocks - Provision services (Food supply, Raw material supply, Water supply), Regulating services (Gas regulation, Climate regulation, Hydrological regulation, Soil formation, Waste treatment) and Supporting services (Soil conservation, Nutrient cycling, Biodiversity, Culture & education). Colour is used as the only row separator: three greens by service block and orange for the two header bands, with no rule anywhere and no legend. THE HEADER BANDS ARE UNREADABLE AT PRINT SIZE: the top band's four merged labels sit at about 4 pt and the second band's twelve sub-type labels overlap each other, so several columns cannot be attributed to a land type. THE GRID IS ALSO SIGNED IN PLACES AND UNSIGNED EXPLANATION: raw material supply carries −0.94, −3.63 and −0.91 and water supply −1.05, i.e. negative per-unit values in a grid the section presents as positive coefficients, and no note says what a negative service value means. Values print at mixed precision (1.36, 0.85, 0.1, 0.38, 0.01, 0) with bare 0 cells, and the '0' column repeats over several land types. Caption prints BELOW. NO SENTENCE NAMES IT: the section moves straight from the standard-equivalent text into the sensitivity formula.

caption.verbatim: Figure 3: the ESV of 14 provinces in China (Billion yuan)

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 3: the ESV of 14 provinces in China (Billion yuan)
items.note: Fourteen provinces by nine columns - Cultivated Land, Woodland, Grassland, Construction Land, Waters, Unutilized land, ESV, Cultivated Land Contributi-on Rate - ruled booktabs, caption '(Billion yuan)'. THE ARITHMETIC HOLDS TO THE LAST DIGIT: for every one of the fourteen rows the six land-type cells sum to the printed ESV (Beijing 21.24 + 437.48 + 30.77 − 67.23 + 12.29 + 0.00 = 434.55), and the contribution rate is the cultivated cell over that sum to two decimals (Jiangsu 448.74/638.72 = 70.26 as printed). THE UNIT IN THE CAPTION CONTRADICTS THE PROSE: if the cells are billions of yuan then Inner Mongolia's ESV of 36235.51 is 36 trillion yuan, while the text says the three highest provinces 'measured by currency amount exceeds 100 billion yuan' - a threshold every one of the fourteen rows passes - and Figure 4 plots the same quantity on an axis marked '*10^8 Yuan', a third scale for the same numbers. THREE HEADER CELLS ARE HYPHENATED ACROSS LINES ('Constructi-on Land', 'Contributi-on Rate'), two stub labels are abbreviations printed nowhere else (IM, Jiln - the second a typo for Jilin), every header in the table carries a trailing full stop, and the column of negative construction-land values (−67.23 through −556.85) is never explained. Caption prints BELOW. NO SENTENCE NAMES THE TABLE: the text reads the values by province without ever calling the grid a figure.

caption.verbatim: Figure 4: Scatter plot comparing the results of two calculations

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 4: Scatter plot comparing the results of two calculations

mention.lead_sentence: get a scatter plot in ﬁgure 4.

items.note: Fourteen black triangles on a full box, our ESV on the abscissa against the published ESV on the ordinate, both titled 'ESV calculated ... /(*10^8 Yuan)'. NO REFERENCE LINE: the claim the plate exists to support - 'the trends of ESV levels calculated by the two methods are consistent' - is read off the diagonal by eye, and no 45-degree line, no regression line, no R squared, no slope and no n are printed anywhere on the plate or in the sentence. THE TWO FORTY-FIVE-DEGREE CASES ARE NOT DISTINGUISHABLE: points sit slightly ABOVE the diagonal at the top (about 200000 against 195000) and slightly BELOW at the bottom, so the two methods do not agree in level and the plate prints nothing that would say by how much. THE ORDINATE IS LABELLED AT THREE TICKS ONLY (50000, 150000, 250000) against six on the abscissa, and neither axis is titled with a quantity - both titles repeat the software's '*10^8' multiplier string, a scale that matches neither Figure 3's caption unit nor any conversion stated in the text. No gridlines and no point labels, so which triangle is which province cannot be recovered from the plate although the prose names four provinces by name. Caption prints BELOW.

caption.verbatim: Figure 5: Ecological service capacity calculated by unit area

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 5: Ecological service capacity calculated by unit area
items.note: Fourteen bars of ESC per unit area, every value printed in a white label above its stem: 306.3, 321.84, 370.40, 323.62, 388.16, 364.59, 273.83, 307.11, 215.81, 194.09, 162.36, 93.95, 264.81, 59.58 against IM, HLJ, Sichuan, Jilin, Jiangxi, Hunan, Liaoning, Hubei, Hebei, Anhui, Henan, SD, Beijing, Jiangsu. THE CHART HAS NO ORDINATE: there are no ticks, no numbers and no baseline on the y axis - only a rotated title 'ESC (Unit area) (10^4 yuan/hm^2)' - so the only quantities on the plate are the fourteen labels and the bar heights carry nothing the labels do not. THE BARS THEMSELVES ARE INVISIBLE: they are drawn as thin white stems on a light blue field, so bar length cannot be compared and the plate reads as a sorted list with decoration. THE ORDER IS NEITHER SORTED NOR GEOGRAPHIC: it runs 306.3, 321.84, 370.40, 323.62 ... so the first three rise before falling, and 264.81 (Beijing) is printed between 93.95 and 59.58. THE UNIT CONTRADICTS THE PROSE BY A FACTOR OF A HUNDRED: section 3.5.3 says Jiangsu and Shandong are 'less than 1 million yuan/km2' and that Jiangxi, Hunan and Sichuan are 'higher than 3.5 million yuan/km2', but the ordinate is printed in 10^4 yuan per HECTARE, where Jiangsu's 59.58 is 0.6 million per hectare and Sichuan's 370.40 is 3.7 million per hectare - the reading only reconciles if the printed 'hm^2' is a slip for km^2. Three categories are unexpanded abbreviations (IM, HLJ, SD) that appear on no other page. Caption prints BELOW. NO SENTENCE NAMES IT: the text under the heading 'By Area' simply reads the numbers.

caption.verbatim: Figure 6: Ecological service capability classiﬁcation

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 6: Ecological service capability classiﬁcation
items.note: A six-band classification strip, three columns - ESC (Unit area) | Grade | Province - with the bands drawn as colour fills and no rule anywhere: <100 Weak Service Ability (Jiangsu, Shandong), 100-200 Relative Weak (Henan, Anhui), 200-300 Medium (Beijing, Hebei, Liaoning), 300-350 Relative Strong (Inner Mongolia, Jilin, Heilongjiang, Hubei), >350 Strong (Jiangxi, Hunan, Sichuan). IT AGREES WITH FIGURE 5 TO THE LAST PROVINCE: every one of the fourteen provinces is filed in the band its Figure 5 value falls in, and none is missing or double-counted, which makes this the one pair of plates in the section that check each other. WHAT IT OMITS IS THE UNIT: the first column prints bare numbers (<100, 100-200, ... >350) with no scale anywhere on the strip, and the reader has to carry Figure 5's ordinate title across to it. THE BANDS OVERLAP AT THEIR BOUNDARIES: '100-200' and '200-300' both own 200, and '200-300' against '300-350' both own 300, so three of the five thresholds are ambiguous and the two provinces nearest to one (Anhui 194.09, Hubei 307.11) sit either side of a boundary that is defined twice. Colour is the only separator and the six fills run from pink through yellow to dark green with no legend keying them. Caption prints BELOW and the text layer welds the following body sentence to its tail ('... and is conducive to ecological balance and sustainable development.'), so the recorded verbatim is the caption line alone.

caption.verbatim: Figure 7: Ecological service capacity calculated by unit GDP

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 7: Ecological service capacity calculated by unit GDP
items.note: Seventeen columns in one region: fourteen GDP bars with a grey plot field, horizontal gridlines and a y axis ticked 0 to 90000 in ten thousands, and beneath them a two-row data table embedded in the same crop - GDP (10^8 yuan) 18128, 15386, 32935, 14777, 18499, 31551, 22247, 32665, 32071, 24408, 40472, 68025, 25669, 77388 and ESC (Unit GDP) 2.00, 0.99, 0.55, 0.41, 0.35, 0.24, 0.18, 0.17, 0.13, 0.11, 0.07, 0.02, 0.02, 0.01, with a two-entry legend at the lower left keying the two rows. THE BARS PLOT THE WRONG QUANTITY: the caption and the citing passage are about 'ecological service capacity calculated by unit GDP', but the bars are GDP, and the ESC column the caption is about has no axis, no bar and no visual encoding at all - it exists only as type in the table - so the ranking the plate shows (Jiangsu highest, IM lowest) is the INVERSE of the ranking the text describes (IM 2.00 highest, Jiangsu 0.01 lowest). THE EMBEDDED LEGEND CANNOT DISCRIMINATE: both swatches are the same blue, so the key distinguishes nothing. The y axis belongs to the GDP row alone while the second row's units (a ratio per 10^8 yuan) appear only as the row stub, and the three abbreviations IM, HLJ and SD are printed unexpanded as on Figure 5. The eight-figure GDP value 77388 is drawn past the last gridline at 90000 without a label. Caption prints BELOW.

caption.verbatim: Figure 8: Rate of Decline of Three Values

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 8: Rate of Decline of Three Values
items.note: Three series over 2011 to 2015 titled 'Rate of Decline', ordinate ticked 0.00% to 0.90% in ten hundredths, legend printed as one horizontal line BELOW the abscissa keying Direct Value (blue), Indirect Value (red) and 'Enabling Value' (green). THE PAPER NAMES THE SAME QUANTITY THREE WAYS: the legend says 'Enabling Value' where the body says 'existence value' and the framework diagram says 'Existing Value'. THE AXIS IS A PERCENTAGE OF SOMETHING UNSTATED and tops out at 0.90% - a rate of decline so small that the three values fall by less than one per cent in five years, while the prose calls the reduction of indirect and existential value 'more serious' and 'at a faster rate'. NO POINTS ARE MARKED AND NO VALUES PRINTED, so every reading is an eyeballed height: the three series sit at roughly 0.33/0.70/0.77 in 2011 and 0.12/0.57/0.55 in 2015, which makes the existential series the one that FALLS FASTEST in absolute points and the direct series the one that falls fastest in relative terms - the plate does not settle which comparison the text means. THE X AXIS HAS NO TITLE OF ITS OWN: the word 'Year' is stranded at the right end of the legend row beneath the plot. No gridlines, no reference line at zero, no note on the base the percentage is taken against. Caption prints BELOW and the crop shows the legend sitting between the art and the caption.

caption.verbatim: Figure 9: The Ratio of ESV of Various E- cosystems

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 9: The Ratio of ESV of Various E- cosystems

mention.lead_sentence: radar map is drawn in ﬁgure 9.

items.note: A radar map: one blue polygon over six spokes - Woodland, Grassland, Waters, Farmland, Construction Land, Unused Land - with five pale concentric rings and radial labels printed along the top spoke reading 1.04, 1.02, 1, 0.96, 0.94, 0.92, 0.9, 0.88. THE RADIAL SCALE SKIPS A STEP: the labels fall by 0.02 except between 1 and 0.96, where the step is 0.04, and 0.98 is absent - so either a ring is missing or one label is misprinted, and the polygon's position against the rings cannot be read by counting. THE REFERENCE VALUE IS NOT DRAWN: the quantity is the ratio of 2015 to 2010 ESV, so a ratio of 1 is the no-change case, but no ring at 1.00 is marked or named and the reader has to find it among eight unlabelled numerals set on top of the Woodland spoke. THE POLYGON ITSELF CARRIES NO INFORMATION BEYOND ITS SHAPE: all six vertices sit between roughly 0.93 and 1.00, an eight-hundredths spread drawn across the whole radius, so the plot makes a nearly circular ring look like a story - while the prose reads it as 'the ESV of the waters and woodland ecosystems has the largest decline' and the plate has no vertex label, no value and no legend entry to identify which vertex is which beyond the spoke name. The spoke labels mix title case ('Construction Land', 'Unused Land') with single-word lower-case names, and the paper calls the same classes 'Unutilized land', 'Waters' and 'Existing Value' elsewhere. Caption prints BELOW and wraps mid-word at 'E-/cosystems', so the recorded verbatim is the caption as the column breaks it. NO OTHER PLATE IN THE PAPER IS A RADAR MAP, so this row records the only 'other' family in the census.
items.other_note: radar (spider) chart - a plot of one polygon over six category spokes, with no slot in the closed family vocabulary

caption.verbatim: Figure 10: Ecosystem services value unit area of different land types in Huangguosh

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 10: Ecosystem services value unit area of different land types in Huangguosh
items.note: A one-row table captioned as a figure: seven land types across the header - Cultivated land 3613.65, Garden plot 7606.45, Woodland 11426.68, Grassland 3786.23, Waters 24040.47, Swamp and tidal flats 32794.82, Other land 219.64 - with the row stub 'Ecological Value per Unit Area ( yuan/(hm^2·a) )'. Colour bands only, no rules, header band filled teal. THE TABLE IS TRANSPOSED AGAINST TABLE 2 AND USES A DIFFERENT CLASS SET: Table 2 has six land types as columns with values as one row, this one has seven as columns with one row as well, but the two class lists share no name except Woodland, Grassland and Waters, so the Yangtze and Huangguoshu valuations cannot be compared; the section's own Figure 21 uses a third set again. THE UNIT STRING IS MALFORMED AND INCONSISTENT: 'yuan/(hm^2·a)' with doubled and spaced parentheses, where Table 2 writes 'yuan/hm2' in its caption and Figure 5 writes '10^4 yuan/hm^2', and the '·a' (per year) appears only here - the caption omits it and says only 'value unit area', which is not grammatical. Precision is uniform at two decimals, the one table in the paper that is. The header cell 'Swamp and tidal flats' wraps to two lines where its six neighbours do not. Caption prints BELOW and a sliver of the preceding prose is inside the top edge of the region. The citing sentence prints the figure reference inside a parenthesis at the end of a sentence - '(see in ﬁgure 10)' - the only place the paper uses this form.

section_path: 4.2.2 Adjustment of the value of ecological services

caption.verbatim: Figure 11: Cost-beneﬁt curve(a)

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 11: Cost-beneﬁt curve(a)

mention.lead_sentence: As shows in ﬁgure 11 and ﬁgure 12:

items.note: A hand-drawn cost-benefit sketch: three straight lines - Total Benefit (grey), Total Cost Including Ecological Costs (red) and Total Cost Without Ecological Costs (blue) - labelled by floating text at their right ends with no legend box, two equilibria marked as yellow dots A and B on the RED line where it meets Total Benefit, dotted verticals dropped to T1 and T2, and a bracket on the lower left labelled 'Ecological Cost' over 'Construction Cost'. THE AXES ARE UNQUANTIFIED: 'Total Cost/Benefi t' is printed horizontally at the top left instead of rotated, 'Time' at the bottom right, and there is not one tick, number, unit or year on either axis - the plate prints no figure at all except the subscripts T1 and T2. THE BRACKET IS UNDIMENSIONED AND UNALIGNED: it is meant to show the gap between the two cost lines, but its ends do not meet either line and no value is given for the ecological cost, so the paper's central distinction between with-and-without ecological cost is drawn as a pair of parallel strokes with a bracket beside them. Both cost lines are drawn as straight parallels rising from the same origin with no justification given, and the blue 'without ecological costs' line never crosses Total Benefit in the frame, so only one of the two cases yields a break-even point on the plate even though the text discusses point A for both. Caption prints BELOW and carries '(a)' while the art carries no panel letter.

caption.verbatim: Figure 12: Cost-beneﬁt curve(b)

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 12: Cost-beneﬁt curve(b)

mention.lead_sentence: As shows in ﬁgure 11 and ﬁgure 12:

items.note: The (b) panel of the same sketch, same three floating labels, same undimensioned cost bracket, one equilibrium A marked - this time on the BLUE line, at its crossing with Total Benefit - with a dotted vertical to T1 and no B and no T2. THE TWO PANELS DO NOT READ AS A CONTROLLED CONTRAST: (a) marks two equilibria on the red with-ecological-cost line and (b) marks one on the blue without-ecological-cost line, so the letter A denotes a different case in each panel and the reader cannot tell what changed between them - whether (b) is a different project, a different period or a different cost assumption is stated nowhere on either plate and nowhere in the sentences reading them. THE RED LINE IS DRAWN STEEPER HERE and starts above the origin, so its crossing with Total Benefit falls outside the plotted region and is left unmarked: the panel that is supposed to show the ecological-cost case is the one where that case's break-even cannot be seen. Same unquantified axes as (a) - no tick, no number, no unit. Caption prints BELOW, carrying '(b)' that the art does not print.

caption.verbatim: Figure 13: the impact of area change in Hei-

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 13: the impact of area change in Hei-
items.note: Heilongjiang's four area-elasticity curves against the percentage change of land area: solid blue 'GDP(ΔA1/A1)', dashed blue 'GDP(ΔA2/A2)', solid red 'ESV(ΔA1/A1)' and a fourth drawn as a dashed red line labelled ... 'GDP(ΔA2/A2)', the same words as the second entry. THE LEGEND NAMES THREE SERIES AND DRAWS FOUR: the fourth entry repeats a label already used and no 'ESV(ΔA2/A2)' entry exists, so one of the four curves is unlabelled and one is labelled twice, and the colouring (red for the pair the paper calls ESV) contradicts the text of the legend. THE AXIS OF THE WHOLE PLATE IS UNQUANTIFIED: the abscissa is titled 'ΔA/A' with ticks from -3% to 3% in whole per cents, and the ordinate carries NO title, NO ticks and NO numbers at all, so 'the impact of forest area change on ESV and GDP is moderate' is read off four unlabelled strokes. NO ZERO RULE IS DRAWN even though all four curves are constructed to pass through ΔA = 0, which is the one point the section reasons about. The A1/A2 subscripts are never defined on the plate or in the caption - the surrounding prose defines A1 as forest land and A2 as residential construction land only in the Jiangsu paragraph that follows. Caption prints BELOW and the caption line itself is broken by the column - the recorded verbatim ends at 'in Hei-', with 'longjiang' carried onto the next line of the same caption.

caption.verbatim: Figure 14: the impact of area change in

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 14: the impact of area change in
items.note: Jiangsu's plot is drawn as TWO STACKED BANDS sharing one abscissa - a blue band of two GDP curves over an orange/yellow band of two ESV curves - with a four-entry legend beneath keying GDP(ΔA2/A2), GDP(ΔA3/A3), ESV(ΔA2/A2) and ESV(ΔA3/A3), abscissa ticks from -3.20% to 3.20% in 0.40% steps. TWO IN-PLOT ANNOTATIONS ARE THE ONLY NUMBERS ON THE PLATE and both check out against the rest of the paper: '77388 (10^8 Yuan)' on the GDP curves is Jiangsu's GDP as printed in Figure 7's table, and '639 (10^8 Yuan)' on the ESV curve is its ESV as printed in Figure 3 (638.72), so the pair are the ΔA = 0 levels and the two figures agree with each other across three pages. NEITHER BAND HAS A SCALE: no ordinate title, no tick and no number on either band, so the shape of each curve is visible while its magnitude exists only at the two annotated points, and the two bands are drawn at unrelated vertical scales inside one frame with nothing saying so. THE TICK LABELS COLLIDE AT THE ORIGIN ('0.00%' and '0.40%' overprint), and the 0.40%-step grid is finer than the -3%/2%/3% grid of Figure 13, so the two provinces' plots are not directly comparable although they are printed as a pair. Caption prints BELOW and is broken by the column in the same way as Figure 13's, the recorded verbatim ending at 'in'.

caption.verbatim: Figure 15: Ecosystem value change chart during the year

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 15: Ecosystem value change chart during the year
items.note: Fifteen monthly series with point markers over months 1 to 12, ordinate 'ESV/10^12 Yuan' ticked 0.0 to 1.5 in halves, legend OUTSIDE at the right in one column of fifteen entries (Paddy Field, Upland Field, Coniferous Forest, Coniferous & Broadleaf, Broadleaf Forest, Shrubwood, Grassland, Shrub Grass, Meadow, Water System, Wetlands, Glacier, Construction Land, Desert, Bare Land). THE LEGEND IS BIGGER THAN THE PLOT AND REPEATS THE PLATE: fifteen entries are listed to identify fifteen curves, most of which lie on top of one another in the 0.0-to-0.2 band for months 1 to 3 and 10 to 12, so the middle of the family cannot be separated by eye and the legend is the only place the categories exist. THE CLAIM THE PLATE IS FOR IS NOT VISIBLE IN IT: the prose reads July as 'the highest point' for every ecosystem, but the abscissa ticks only at 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12, so the July values fall between two labelled ticks and the peak cannot be located on the axis without counting markers. THE EXPONENT IS TYPESET AS A CARET: 'ESV/10^12 Yuan' prints the power as plain text rather than as a superscript, the third unit convention for the same quantity in the paper. No gridlines, no data labels, no reference line, and the category list here again differs from Figure 2's and Table 2's sets. Caption prints BELOW.

caption.verbatim: Figure 16: The table of Different ecosystem importance levels

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 16: The table of Different ecosystem importance levels
items.note: THE CAPTION CALLS IT A TABLE AND THE ART IS A LINE CHART: 'Figure 16: The table of Different ecosystem importance levels' sits under six marker-coded series on an ordinate titled 'IMPORTANCE' ticked 0 to 0.5 in 0.05 steps and an abscissa titled 'YEARS/YR' ticked 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024 and 2028, legend above the plot in two rows of three (Woodland, Grassland, Arable land, Wetlands, Waters, Unutilized land). IT IS THE ONLY PLATE IN THE PAPER WHOSE CAPTION DESCRIBES A DIFFERENT EXHIBIT FROM THE ONE DRAWN, and the section text reinforces the error, saying the importance is 'calculated according to the following formula' and then that the reader will 'obtain the importance level table'. THE ABSCISSA RUNS FOUR YEARS PAST THE DATA: the sources are 2004, 2008, 2012 and 2016 and the grey prediction adds 2020 to 2028, but no marker style, line style, shading or legend entry distinguishes a predicted point from an observed one, so the forecast the section is about is not identifiable on the plate. Category names drift again ('Arable land' here for the 'Cultivated land' of Figures 17 and 22), the ordinate's top tick at 0.5 sits a fifth above the highest series, and no gridlines or data labels are printed. Caption prints BELOW.

caption.verbatim: Figure 17: Land Use Changes of Yangtze River Delta,2010-2015

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 17: Land Use Changes of Yangtze River Delta,2010-2015
items.note: A printed table under a figure number - two header rows (Year | a merged 'Land Use Type' over the six type columns), six year rows 2010 to 2015, then '2010-2015 Area Change' and '2010-2015 Change Rate' - ruled booktabs with no verticals and no colour. NO UNIT IS PRINTED ANYWHERE: not in the header, not in the caption, not in the change row, so whether the cells are km2, hm2 or 10^4 hectares cannot be recovered from the plate or from any page of the paper. caption.verbatim: Figure 18: Changes of Ecosystem Service Value of Yangtze River Delta,2010-2015

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 18: Changes of Ecosystem Service Value of Yangtze River Delta,2010-2015
items.note: The companion table: Year | six land types | Total, six year rows 2010 to 2015, then the ESV change and change-rate rows, booktabs with no verticals, caption below. CONSTRUCTION LAND CARRIES A NEGATIVE SERVICE VALUE throughout (-860.68 falling to -920.00) with no note on the sign convention, while its change rate prints as a positive +6.89% - a mixing of sign conventions inside one row that the plate does not explain. THE TWO RATES THAT CAN BE RECOMPUTED FROM THE CELLS DISAGREE WITH THE PLATE: unused land 2.16 to 2.22 is +2.78% where 2.65% is printed (the 2.65% being Figure 17's LAND-AREA rate), and the Total column does not tie to its own row sums at 2014 (5454.23 printed against 5454.21 summed) and 2015 (5426.55 against 5426.53). Precision drifts inside the table - grassland's rate prints -6.8% here and -6.80% in Figure 17 - and the caption carries 'Delta,2010-2015' in the text layer as a separate heading line above it. NO UNIT IS STATED for the million-scale columns although Figure 19, four pages later, prints the same quantity in 'Million Yuan'. Caption prints BELOW.

caption.verbatim: Figure 19: Changes of Three Values of Yangtze River Delta,2010-2015

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 19: Changes of Three Values of Yangtze River Delta,2010-2015
items.note: Three value columns and a year stub - Direct Value, Indirect Value, Existing Value, each headed 'Million Yuan' on a second header line - over the years 2010 to 2015 and the change and change-rate rows, ruled booktabs, caption below. THE FIRST ROW'S ARITHMETIC IS OFF BY A UNIT IN THE LAST PLACE: direct value falls 390.026 to 383.314, a change of -6.712, printed -6.713, and -6.712/390.026 is -1.721% against a printed -1.72%. The other two columns reconcile exactly (-118.515 and -3.23%, -51.790 and -3.35%), so this is a single mis-keyed digit rather than a modelling error. THE HEADER SPLITS ITS OWN UNIT ACROSS A STRAY SLASH ('Direct Value/' then 'Million Yuan'), and the change row carries no unit at all while the rate row carries only '%'. Three columns at three decimals against the two decimals of every other table in the paper, and the caption prints 'Delta,2010-2015' as a separate line above it in the text layer.

caption.verbatim: Figure 20: Coefﬁcient of Sensitivity of Yangtze River Delta,2010-2015

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 20: Coefﬁcient of Sensitivity of Yangtze River Delta,2010-2015
items.note: Six coefficients of sensitivity by land type over 2010 to 2015, five decimals, under a merged header 'Land Use Type (Coefficient of Sensitivity)' that repeats the caption. THEY DO NOT BEHAVE LIKE A DECOMPOSITION: the six coefficients sum to 1.30799, 1.31640, 1.33617, 1.30958, 1.30316 and 1.33425 across the six years - never 1 - so either the metric is not the normalised elasticity the caption names or the entries are wrong, and no definition of CS accompanies the grid. MOST OF THE GRID IS REPEATED VERBATIM: woodland prints 0.40621 in four of the six years and 0.43462 in the other two, waters prints 0.59867 in four, farmland 0.14506 in three - a seven-row annual elasticity table in which more than half the cells are copies of a neighbour, which no computation over changing annual ESV would produce. Category spellings drift from the neighbouring tables ('Unused land' here against 'Unused Land' in Figure 22; 'Unused land' also wraps onto two lines). Caption prints BELOW.

caption.verbatim: Figure 21: The dynamic change of land use in Huangguoshu from 2009 to 2012

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 21: The dynamic change of land use in Huangguoshu from 2009 to 2012
items.note: Eight land types in a three-column grid - land type | 'Amount of Change' | 'Land Use Dynamics' - ruled booktabs. THE TWO QUANTITIES ARE DEFINED NOWHERE: the change column carries no unit (hm2? km2? hectares?) and the dynamics column carries no per-cent sign although it is plainly a rate, and the base areas that would make the rate checkable are not printed, so no cell of the second column can be verified from the plate. The change column does sum exactly to 0.00, so the area flows balance across the eight classes, and swamp and tidal flats are the one class at 0.00 in both columns. Construction land is the only positive change of size (+33.88, 4.69) against cultivated land +32.81 and losses in grassland (-43.86), woodland (-21.54) and garden plot (-2.99), which is the paper's story in one grid. The caption omits the 2009-to-2012 span the table covers, prints 'Swamp and Tidal Flats' wrapped across two lines, and the crop truncates the caption at both ends.

caption.verbatim: Figure 22: The total ESV of different land types in Huangguoshu

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 22: The total ESV of different land types in Huangguoshu
items.note: Seven land types by four years - 'Ecological Service Value' merged over 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012 - plus an 'Ecological Cost of the Project' column and a Total row, booktabs, caption below. THE 2009 COLUMN DOES NOT TIE TO ITS OWN TOTAL: the seven ESV cells sum to 9888.22 against a printed Total of 9843.22, a shortfall of exactly 45.00, while 2010, 2011 and 2012 reconcile to within a hundredth; and the cost column sums to 31.99 against a printed 32.03, the gap being exactly the Other Land entry, so Other Land is left out of its own total. THE HEADLINE NUMBER IN THE PROSE DOES NOT COME FROM THIS TABLE: section 4.2.3 says the project 'caused the total value of its ecological service value to drop by 323,300 yuan in four years', and the table's total row falls from 9843.22 to 9811.19, a drop of 32.03 in whatever unit the cells carry, which is 320,300 yuan if the unit is 10^4 - a unit the table never prints. The largest class is woodland at 68.4% of the 2009 total, which is what the prose's 'nearly 70%' refers to, and the ranking cultivated, waters, garden behind it also holds. Waters jumps from 502.76 to 502.78 to 467.37 and back to 502.33 in four consecutive years, a swing of 35 that no land-use change in Figure 21 accounts for. Caption prints BELOW.

caption.verbatim: Figure 23: CS of ecosystem services value of different land types in Huangguoshu

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 23: CS of ecosystem services value of different land types in Huangguoshu
items.note: The coefficient of sensitivity by land type for the same four years, four decimals, under a merged 'Coefficient of Sensitivity (CS)' header, booktabs, caption below. THE SEVEN COEFFICIENTS DO NOT CLOSE: they sum to 0.9971, 0.9970, 0.9970 and 0.9978 in 2009 to 2012, just short of unity in every year, which is the behaviour of a share decomposition with a term dropped. THEY ALSO DO NOT REPRODUCE FROM FIGURE 22'S OWN NUMBERS: cultivated land's 2009 share is 1268.91/9843.22 = 0.1289 against a printed 0.1285, and its 2011 share is 1282.53/9789.07 = 0.1310 against a printed 0.1306, so the two Huangguoshu tables disagree at the third decimal although both are printed to four. THE SAME SYMBOL MEANS A DIFFERENT THING IN THE OTHER APPENDIX TABLE: the Yangtze delta coefficients of Figure 20 sum to about 1.31, these sum to about 0.997, so 'CS' is defined one way for one project and another way for the other while the caption uses the bare initials. Other Land prints 0.0029 to four decimals in all four years while its ESV moves at the second decimal, a flat line no annual recomputation would produce. No unit, no definition, no total row. Caption prints BELOW, clipped at both ends in the crop.

note:
Paper 180, Team 1902029: an ecological-service-value assessment for problem E 2019. A valuation model
built on standard equivalents, two worked projects (the Yangtze River Delta and the Huangguoshu Scenic
Area), a multi-objective land-use programme, and two time-scale studies (seasonal and annual).
Twenty-eight pages, twenty-five measured regions over sixteen of them, resolving into TWENTY-THREE
FIGURE ROWS and TWO TABLE ROWS, with no refusal and nothing unaccounted.

THE CENSUS IS MOSTLY TABLES. Eleven of the twenty-three figure rows are printed grids carrying a
figure number - Figure 2 (a fourteen-column value-coefficient grid with two header bands), Figure 3
(fourteen provinces by nine columns), Figure 6 (a six-band classification strip with no rules, only
colour fills), Figure 10 (one row of seven Huangguoshu values), and the whole appendix block Figures 17
to 23 (land use, ESV, three values, sensitivity for the delta, land-use dynamics, ESV and sensitivity
for Huangguoshu). Two more grids are numbered as tables: Table 1 (the notation list) and Table 2 (six
land-use values in a single unlabelled row). So the paper prints nine exhibit grids against fourteen
drawn plates, and its own prose calls Figure 16 a table while the plate under that caption is a chart.

THE ARITHMETIC IS WHERE THE PAPER IS STRONGEST AND WHERE IT FAILS. Figure 3 is exact: all fourteen
rows' six land-type cells sum to the printed ESV and the cultivated-contribution column is the
cultivated cell over that sum. Figure 6 files all fourteen provinces into the band their Figure 5 value
falls in, with none missing or doubled. Figure 14's two in-plot annotations are Jiangsu's GDP and ESV as
printed in Figures 7 and 3, so the same numbers agree across three pages. Against that: Figure 17 prints
a 0.79 change where the endpoints give 0.78, Figure 18's unused-land rate is computed from Figure 17's
land-area change rather than from its own ESV cells, Figure 19's direct-value change is off by a unit in
the last decimal, Figure 22's 2009 column sums to 9888.22 against a printed total of 9843.22 (a 45.00
shortfall) and its ecological-cost column to 31.99 against 32.03 (the gap being the Other Land entry),
and the two sensitivity grids do not close - 1.31 for the delta, 0.997 for Huangguoshu - while both are
called CS.

UNITS ARE THE PAPER'S WORST HABIT. One quantity appears as "Billion yuan" (Figure 3's caption), "*10^8
Yuan" (Figure 4's axes), "10^4 yuan/hm^2" (Figure 5's ordinate), "yuan/km2" (the prose that reads Figure
5, which only reconciles if the printed hm^2 is a slip for km^2), "Million Yuan" (Figure 19) and
"ESV/10^12 Yuan" (Figure 15, with the exponent set as a caret). Figure 7's caption names a quantity per
unit GDP and its bars plot GDP. Figures 17 and 18 print no unit at all.

THE DRAWN PLATES. Figure 1 is a five-rank framework whose Support Service box is routed into the value
layer although the text deliberately excludes it. Figure 4 is a fourteen-point scatter with no identity
or regression line and an ordinate labelled at three ticks against the abscissa's six. Figures 5 and 7
are bar charts without usable ordinates - Figure 5's bars are thin white stems on a light field with no
ticks at all, Figure 7's legend keys two rows with the same blue swatch. Figure 8 is a three-series
decline chart topping out at 0.90% with its x-axis title stranded in the legend row, and Figure 9 is the
paper's only radar map, a near-regular hexagon over an eight-step radial scale that skips 0.98 and marks
no ring at 1.00. Figures 11 and 12 are hand-drawn cost-benefit sketches with no tick, no number and no
unit on either axis; (a) marks two equilibria A and B and (b) marks one, and the same letter A denotes a
different line in the two panels. Figures 13 and 14 are area-elasticity plots with no ordinate scale,
Figure 13's legend naming three series and drawing four. Figure 15 is fifteen monthly series whose
legend is larger than the plot. Figure 16 is the chart captioned as a table. Figure 21, though it sits in
the appendix beside the project's land-use discussion, is another printed table - eight land types with
a change column and a dynamics column, neither of which carries a unit.

ONLY TWO OF THE TWENTY-FIVE REGIONS ARE LIVE TEXT. The layout pass reports Table 1 (p5) and Table 2
(p14) as three-path vectors and EVERY OTHER REGION AS A SINGLE-PATH RASTER, so twenty-three exhibits -
the framework diagram, every chart, and all seven appendix tables - were pasted into the document as
images: the typesetting of those grids is not the paper's own, their fonts and decimal points are not
the body's, and none of their numerals can be selected or re-set. That is also why a paper about land
use prints no map: the GIS output the appendix refers to was never reproduced as a plate, only
tabulated.

Families: table-as-figure 11, line 5 (Figures 8, 13, 14, 15, 16), flowchart-or-schematic 3 (Figures 1,
11, 12), bar 2 (Figures 5, 7), scatter 1 (Figure 4), other 1 (Figure 9, the radar map), table-grid 2.
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: twenty-five measured regions over sixteen of twenty-eight pages resolve into twenty-three figure rows and two table rows, with no refusal and nothing unaccounted [place.doc_order].
A caption can promise a table and be printed over a chart: Figure 16 is captioned 'The table of Different ecosystem importance levels' and is a six-series line chart [caption.verbatim].

A figure number can sit over a printed table: eleven of the twenty-three figure rows are tables - Figures 2, 3, 6, 10, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 - and the paper's own prose calls the last of them 'the importance level table' while numbering it a figure [geometry.family].
The appendix is a plate block: Figures 17 to 23 sit on three pages with no sentence of prose anywhere near them, so the last seven rows of the census are named by nothing [mention.count].

Region order is not reading order: on p15 the Figure 9 radar occupies region 1 and the Figure 8 line chart region 2, and on p20 the Figure 13 and Figure 14 plots are likewise exchanged, both settled from the crop and not from the region index [place.page_order].

One quantity is printed in four unit systems: 'Billion yuan' in Figure 3's caption, '*10^8 Yuan' on Figure 4's axes, '10^4 yuan/hm^2' on Figure 5's ordinate, 'yuan/km2' in the prose that reads it, and 'Million Yuan' and 'ESV/10^12 Yuan' later still [caption.verbatim].

A chart can plot the quantity its caption is not about: Figure 7's bars are GDP while the caption names the ecological service capacity per unit GDP, which exists only as an unplotted row in the table beneath the bars, so the plate's ranking is the inverse of the text's [geometry.legend].
A legend can name three series and draw four: Figure 13 keys GDP(ΔA1/A1), GDP(ΔA2/A2) and ESV(ΔA1/A1) and then prints GDP(ΔA2/A2) a second time over the fourth curve [geometry.legend].
Axes can be drawn with no scale at all: Figures 11 and 12 carry no tick, no number and no unit on either axis, and Figures 13 and 14 carry none on the ordinate [geometry.family].

A table can fail its own arithmetic: Figure 17 prints a 0.79 change where 30.49 against 29.71 gives 0.78, Figure 18's unused-land rate is 2.78% computed against a printed 2.65%, Figure 19's first change is -6.713 where the endpoints give -6.712, Figure 22's 2009 column sums to 9888.22 against a printed 9843.22 and its cost column to 31.99 against 32.03, and Figures 20 and 23 print sensitivity grids that sum to 1.31 and 0.997 respectively [geometry.printed_numbers].

Three value types are named four ways: 'Existing Value' in the framework diagram, 'existential value' in the prose, 'Enabling Value' in Figure 8's legend and 'Indirect Value' for the middle class throughout [caption.verbatim].

caption.verbatim: Table 1: List of Notations

tables.note: Two columns, Symbol | Deﬁnition, ten body rows from ESV and A_k down to I_ij, ruled booktabs - a rule above the header, a rule under it and a rule at the foot, no verticals. THE SYMBOL COLUMN MIXES TWO REGISTERS: ESV, CS, ESC and GDP are set in roman capitals while A_k, VC_k, E_ak and I_ij are italic with subscripts, so the same column carries both word-abbreviations and algebra and the reader cannot tell an operator from a token. Two of the ten rows wrap their definition onto a second line (the CS row and the I_ij row), and the CS definition prints its parenthesis unclosed-upon a space - 'Coefficient of Sensitivity(ESV sensitivity to VC)' - with no space before the bracket. FIVE SYMBOLS USED IN THE BODY ARE NOT DEFINED HERE: the model writes ESC_i = ESV_i/A_i, ESV_i, ESV_j, VC_ik and VC_jk, and only the unsubscripted stems appear; and 'I_ij' is listed as 'The value of land type j in all land types in the year i' which is the importance level of section 6, not the notation of section 1.3. Caption prints ABOVE. NO SENTENCE NAMES THE TABLE: the body writes the bare heading '1.3 notation' and the grid follows.

caption.verbatim: Table 2: Ecosystem Service Value(yuan/hm2) of Land Use Type in Yangtze River Delta

tables.caption_verbatim: Table 2: Ecosystem Service Value(yuan/hm2) of Land Use Type in Yangtze River Delta
tables.note: One data row across six land types - Woodland 37979.23, Grassland 12584.42, Farmland 12000.82, Wetland 108001.3, Waters 79956.43, Unutilized land 734.44 yuan/hm2 - ruled booktabs, caption above with the unit set in italic inside the caption rather than in a header. THE ROW HAS NO STUB: there is no leftmost label saying whose values these are, so the single row is named only by the caption's 'of Land Use Type in Yangtze River Delta' and holds six numbers with nothing to hang them on - not a year, not a scenario, not a per-unit-area or per-total distinction. PRECISION IS INCONSISTENT: five cells print two decimals and Wetland prints 108001.3, one decimal. The land-type classes disagree with the three other land-type listings in the paper - the appendix plates use Cultivated land, Garden plot, Swamp and tidal flats and Other land, and Figure 2 uses fourteen sub-types - so the six values cannot be matched against the ESV plates they are supposed to feed. Caption prints ABOVE; cited once by 'Value(yuan/hm2) of Land Use Type' context only, the sentence 'the unit area value table of different land use types can be calculated' naming no table.
